{{nihongo|'''Inbe Shrine'''|忌部神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Awa Province (Tokushima)]].

=== History ===
In the ``Kogo Shui'' section of the ritual utensils section, {{ill|Amatomi no Mikoto|Q24899653|qid=Q24899653}}, the grandchild of Tentadama no Mikoto, is shown as a grain tree and {{ill|Q79817 In search of suitable land to plant|qid=Q79817 In search of suitable land to plant|lt=hemp}}, the Ibe clan of Awa led the grandsons of Hiwasi no Mikoto to {{ill|Awa Province (Tokushima)|Q907457|qid=Q907457}} and settled there. |Q11433653}} It is written that cotton and {{ill|Hemp cloth|Q11239515|qid=Q11239515|lt=linen cloth}} came to be offered as tribute, but after that, the rough cloth woven by Mr. It was customary to offer Aratae Miso (aratae miso). In addition, on the mountainside called "Kuroiwa" behind this shrine, there is the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Ibeyama Kofun Group}}, which consists of five {{ill|Round Kofun|Q11394747|qid=Q11394747}} that are believed to have been built in the latter half of the 6th century. This suddenly appeared around the 6th century, and it has been pointed out that there may have been a clan group that immigrated to the area. <ref> Tokushima Prefectural Museum, ed. "Awa no Inabe clan", Tokushima Prefectural Museum, 1977. </ref>.According to the shrine's legend, it began when the Inabe clan of Awa enshrined their ancestor Tenhiwashi no Mikoto on February 25th (lunar calendar)|Q839178|February 25th}} in the second year of {{ill|Emperor Jimmu|Q200188|qid=Q200188}}, and it is said that it was originally enshrined at the above-mentioned ``Kuroiwa''. Since ancient times, it has been known as the {{ill|Ujigami|Q767655|qid=Q767655}} from the Awaimbe clan, and also {{ill|Daidō|de|Daidō (Ära)|es|Daidō|fa|دایدو (دوره)|fr|Ère Daidō|ia|Daido|id|Daidō|ja|大同 (日本)|ko|다이도 (일본)|ru|Дайдо (нэнго)|simple|Daidō|sr|Даидо|th|ไดโด|tr|Daidō|uk|Дайдо|zh|大同 (日本)|zh_yue|大同 (日本)|qid=Q1373191|lt=Datong}} In the first year ({{ill|806|ab|806|af|806|als|806|am|806 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|806|ar|806|ary|806|ast|806|az|806|azb|۸۰۶ (میلادی)|bar|806|bcl|806|be|806|be_x_old|806|bg|806|bn|৮০৬|bpy|মারি ৮০৬|br|806|bs|806.|ca|806|cdo|806 nièng|ceb|806|ckb|٨٠٦|crh|806|cs|806|csb|806|cv|806|cy|806|da|806|de|806|el|806|eml|806|eo|806|es|806|et|806|eu|806|fa|۸۰۶ (میلادی)|fi|806|fo|806|fr|806|frr|806|fy|806|ga|806|gan|806年|gd|806|gl|806|he|806|hi|806|hr|806.|ht|806 (almanak jilyen)|hu|806|hy|806|id|806|ilo|806|io|806|is|806|it|806|ja|806年|jv|806|ka|806|kaa|806|kk|806 жыл|ko|806년|la|806|lb|806|lij|806|lmo|806|lt|806 m.|lv|806. gads|map_bms|806|mdf|806|mg|806|mhr|806|mk|806|mr|इ.स. ८०६|mrj|806 и|ms|806|mzn|۸۰۶|nah|806|nap|806|nds|806|new|सन् ८०६|nl|806|nn|806|no|806|nrm|806|nso|806|oc|806|or|୮୦୬|os|806-æм аз|pl|806|pt|806|qu|806|ro|806|ru|806 год|rue|806|sa|८०६|scn|806|sd|806ع|se|806|sh|806.|shn|806|si|806|sk|806|sl|806|smn|806|sq|806|sr|806|su|806|sv|806|sw|806|tg|Соли 806|th|พ.ศ. 1349|tk|806|tl|806|tly|806|tr|806|tt|806 ел|uk|806|ur|806ء|uz|806|vec|806|vi|806|vls|806|war|806|wuu|806年|xmf|806|zh|806年|zh_min_nan|806 nî|zh_yue|806年|qid=Q30021}}), there were 20 houses. ('{{ill|Shinshō Kyakuchokufushō|ja|新抄格勅符抄|qid=Q11502312}}'), so it seems that he was respected by the imperial court, but the details are unknown. According to the company journal, in the medieval period, in the first year of {{ill|Bunji (era)|Q1194415|qid=Q1194415}} ({{ill|1185|Q19729|qid=Q19729}}), {{ill|Kawano Michinobu|Q11554270|qid=Q11554270}} was published by {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Nagamitsu}}, and during the {{ill|Battle of Yashima|Q2117322|qid=Q2117322}}, {{ill|Minamoto no Yoshitsune|Q310445|qid=Q310445}} and {{ill|Nasu no Yoichi|Q2625800|qid=Q2625800}} dedicated swords and bows and arrows to pray for victory. , the following year, in the 3rd year of the Bunji era, {{ill|Nariyoshi Taguchi|Q11576353|qid=Q11576353}} was ordered by {{ill|Minamoto no Yoritomo|Q242800|qid=Q242800}} to {{ill|Itano District, Tokushima|Q1156025|qid=Q1156025|lt=Bando/Bandishi}} and {{ill|Q48 29634|qid=Q48 29634|lt=Awa}} and {{ill|Miyoshi District, Tokushima|Q1156031|qid=Q1156031|lt=Miyoshi}}, 1,000 towns of rice fields were carved out and donated as offerings to the 4 districts, conveying the reverence of the samurai <ref> Included in Asae County Magazine (1922) edited by the Asae County Educational Association. </ref>. Also, according to the company journal ``Yamazaki Saibe Shrine Chronicles,'' it collapsed to its current location due to an earthquake in the {{ill|Ōei|Q1193078|qid=Q1193078}} years (1394-1428), and was enshrined as a small shrine next to the Oji Gongen, which was at its current location. </ref>. (Tsurugi Town)|Q119929720|Gosho Shrine}} There was a counterargument, and in the same year 7 ({{ill|1874|ab|1874|af|1874|als|1874|am|1874 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|1874|ar|1874|ary|1874|arz|1874|ast|1874|avk|1874|az|1874|azb|۱۸۷۴ (میلادی)|ba|1874 йыл|ban|1874|bar|1874|bat_smg|1874|bcl|1874|be|1874|be_x_old|1874|bg|1874|bn|১৮৭৪|bpy|মারি ১৮৭৪|br|1874|bs|1874.|ca|1874|cdo|1874 nièng|ce|1874 шо|ceb|1874|ckb|١٨٧٤|crh|1874|cs|1874|csb|1874|cv|1874|cy|1874|da|1874|de|1874|diq|1874|el|1874|eml|1874|eo|1874|es|1874|et|1874|eu|1874|fa|۱۸۷۴|fi|1874|fiu_vro|1874|fo|1874|fr|1874|frp|1874|frr|1874|fur|1874|fy|1874|ga|1874|gan|1874年|gcr|1874|gd|1874|gl|1874|gn|1874|gv|1874|hak|1874-ngièn|he|1874|hi|१८७४|hif|1874|hr|1874.|hsb|1874|ht|1874 (almanak gregoryen)|hu|1874|hy|1874|hyw|1874 թուական|ia|1874|id|1874|ilo|1874|io|1874|is|1874|it|1874|ja|1874年|jv|1874|ka|1874|kaa|1874|kk|1874 жыл|kn|೧೮೭೪|ko|1874년|krc|1874 джыл|ksh|Joohr 1874|ku|1874|kv|1874-ӧд во|la|1874|lb|1874|lez|1874 йис|li|1874|lij|1874|lmo|1874|lt|1874 m.|lv|1874. gads|mai|१८७४|map_bms|1874|mdf|1874|mg|1874|mhr|1874|mi|1874|min|1874|mk|1874|mr|इ.स. १८७४|mrj|1874 и|ms|1874|my|၁၈၇၄|myv|1874 ие|mzn|۱۸۷۴|nah|1874|nap|1874|nds|1874|nds_nl|1874|new|ई सं १८७४|nl|1874|nn|1874|no|1874|nrm|1874|nso|1874|oc|1874|olo|1874|or|୧୮୭୪|os|1874-æм аз|pa|1874|pl|1874|pms|1874|pnb|1874|pt|1874|qu|1874|ro|1874|ru|1874 год|rue|1874|sa|१८७४|sah|1874|scn|1874|sd|1874ع|se|1874|sh|1874.|shn|1874|simple|1874|sk|1874|sl|1874|smn|1874|sq|1874|sr|1874|stq|1874|su|1874|sv|1874|sw|1874|szl|1874|ta|1874|tay|kawas na 1874|te|1874|tet|1874|tg|Соли 1874|th|พ.ศ. 2417|tk|1874|tl|1874|tly|1874|tr|1874|tt|1874 ел|udm|1874 ар|uk|1874|ur|1874ء|uz|1874|vec|1874|vi|1874|vls|1874|vo|1874|wa|1874|war|1874|wuu|1874年|xmf|1874|yi|1874|za|1874 nienz|zea|1874|zh|1874年|zh_classical|一八七四年|zh_min_nan|1874 nî|zh_yue|1874年|qid=Q7761}}), the shrine was re-identified. === Company name ===
Before {{ill|Meiji era|ar|فترة مييجي|ast|Dómina Meiji|az|Meydzi dövrü|azb|مئی‌جی دؤورو|be|Перыяд Мэйдзі|bn|মেইজি যুগ|bo|མེའི་ཇིའི་དུས་དུས་མཚམས།|ca|Era Meiji|cs|Období Meidži|da|Meiji-perioden|de|Meiji-Zeit|el|Μεϊτζί (περίοδος)|es|Era Meiji|et|Meiji periood|eu|Meiji Aroa|fa|دوره میجی|fi|Meiji-kausi|fr|Ère Meiji|gl|Período Meiji|he|תקופת מייג'י|hr|Meiji (razdoblje)|ht|Epòk Meiji|hu|Meidzsi-kor|id|Zaman Meiji|io|Ero Meiji|is|Meiji-tímabilið|it|Periodo Meiji|ja|明治|ka|მეიძის ეპოქა|kbp|Mejii wɛɛ yaa alɩwaatʊ|kk|Мэйдзи дәуірі|ko|메이지 시대|la|Aetas Meiji|lt|Meidži laikotarpis|lv|Meidzi periods|mk|Меиџи (период)|mn|Мэйжийн эрин|ms|Zaman Meiji|nl|Meijiperiode|nn|Meiji|no|Meiji-perioden|pl|Meiji (okres)|pt|Era Meiji|ro|Perioada Meiji|ru|Мэйдзи|simple|Meiji period|sk|Obdobie Meidži|sq|Periudha Meixhi|sr|Меиџи период|sv|Meijiperioden|ta|மெய்சி காலம்|th|ยุคเมจิ|tl|Panahong Meiji|tr|Meiji Dönemi|uk|Період Мейдзі|ur|میجی دور|vi|Thời kỳ Minh Trị|war|Panahon Meiji|wuu|明治|zh|明治|zh_classical|明治|zh_min_nan|Bêng-tī|zh_yue|明治|qid=Q3125096}}, it was called "Tenhiwashi Shrine". Furthermore, as will be explained later, since it was enshrined within the precincts of {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Oji Gongen}}, in early modern times it was simply written as ``''Oji Gongen''''.

=== Shrine building ===
The main shrine has a {{ill|Kirizuma-style|Q13308575|qid=Q13308575}} flat shingled roof, and {{ill|chigi and katsuogi|Q87220234|qid=Q87220234}} is placed on the ridge. According to the ridge tag, it was rebuilt in the 7th year of Kyoho ({{ill|1722|Q6918|qid=Q6918}}).

=== Others ===
In the precincts there is the ``Ruin of the Manfuku Oriden'', which is said to be the remains of the loom where the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Miki clan}} (Mitsukishi}}, who are descendants of the Awa-Ibe clan, wove rough clothes for the Daijo festival.

=== Enshrined God ===
In the note for ``Ibe Shrine'' in ``{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}}'', it says ``A certain name: Asushoku-kami. A certain name: Tenhi-washi-kami.'', which indicates that it is ``Mashoku-kami'' (Oen-kami), also known as {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Amani-washi-kami}}, but the current deities enshrined are as follows.
; {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Tenhiwashi Shoya no Mikoto}}
: He is the {{ill|Oyagami|Q85882782|qid=Q85882782}} of Awa {{ill|Inbe clan|fa|خاندان اینبه|ja|忌部氏|pl|Inbe (ród)|simple|Inbe clan|th|ตระกูลอิมเบะ|zh|忌部氏|qid=Q8189229}} at this shrine {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=main enshrined deity}}.
; Empress Iirame no Mikoto
: Even if it is the second deity of the main enshrined deity, I can't see anything else. <br>
; {{ill|Futodama|it|Futodama|ja|フトダマ|ru|Футодама|simple|Futodama|zh|布刀玉命|qid=Q11059539|lt=Tenta Gyokuson}}
: He is {{ill|Oyagami|Q85882782|qid=Q85882782}} of {{ill|Inbe clan|fa|خاندان اینبه|ja|忌部氏|pl|Inbe (ród)|simple|Inbe clan|th|ตระกูลอิมเบะ|zh|忌部氏|qid=Q8189229}}.
; Empress {{ill|Ame no Hiratome|Q85879124|qid=Q85879124|lt=Hiri Noume no Mikoto}} (Hirinome no Mikoto)
: She is the dowager god of Tenta Tamason (see {{ill|Susaki Shrine|Q11556513|qid=Q11556513}} and {{ill|Sunomiya Shrine|Q11556507|qid=Q11556507}}). <br>
; Tsukuimino Mikoto: ``{{ill|Kogo Shūi|Q531555|qid=Q531555}}'' {{ill|Amaterasu|Q455602|qid=Q455602}}'s {{ill|Amano-Iwato|Q3231835|qid=Q3231835|lt=Amaniwa Cave}}, along with the heavenly eagle-no-mikoto, planted a {{ill|Paper mulberry|an|Broussonetia papyrifera|ar|توت الورق|arz|بروسونته ورقيه|az|Kağız kağızağacı|azb|کاغیزی آغاج|be|Broussonetia papyrifera|ca|Morera de paper|ceb|Broussonetia papyrifera|cs|Papírovník čínský|de|Papiermaulbeerbaum|el|Βρουσονέτια η παπυροφόρος|es|Broussonetia papyrifera|eu|Paper-masustondo|fa|توت کاغذی|fi|Paperimulperio|fr|Broussonetia papyrifera|he|תות נייר|hu|Kínai papíreperfa|hy|Բրուսոնեթիա թղթյա|id|Daluang|it|Broussonetia papyrifera|ja|カジノキ|ko|꾸지나무|la|Broussonetia papyrifera|lfn|Morero turces|mad|Dhâlubâng|mi|Aute|mk|Broussonetia papyrifera|ml|പേപ്പർ മൾബെറി|ms|Jeluang|my|သာလဲပင်|nl|Papiermoerbei|no|Papirmorbærtre|pl|Brusonecja chińska|pt|Amoreira-do-papel|pwn|quljicaca|ru|Бруссонетия бумажная|simple|Paper mulberry|sr|Дудовац|su|Daluang|sv|Pappersmullbärsträd|th|ปอสา|tl|Papel moras|to|Hiapo|tr|Broussonetia papyrifera|uk|Broussonetia papyrifera|vi|Dướng|war|Broussonetia papyrifera|zh|構樹|zh_min_nan|Lo̍k-á-chhiū|zh_yue|構樹|qid=Q389185|lt=grain tree}} and {{ill|cotton (Yuu)|ja|木綿 (ゆう)|qid=Q11519320}}, but there is also a legend that it is another name for ``Kannabihikojin'', the child deity of the sun and eagle life, and the enshrined deity of {{ill|Ōasahiko Shrine|Q723417|qid=Q723417}}<ref>{{ill|Shimotate Matsubara Shrine|Q11361262|qid=Q11361262}} (Takiguchi, Shirahama-cho, Minamiboso City, Chiba Prefecture), the Inabe clan genealogy is handed down in the former {{ill|Shake (social class)|Q11588367|qid=Q11588367}} of {{ill|Awa Shrine|Q705547|qid=Q705547}} (Tateyama City, Chiba Prefecture).
; {{ill|Nagashirahano no Kami|Q11653519|qid=Q11653519|lt=Nagashiraha no Mikoto}}
: Similarly, it can be seen on the steps of Amaterasu Omikami's ghostly residence in the Tengan Cave in the Kogo Shui, and is said to be the ancestral deity of the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Masatsugu clan}} of {{ill|Ise Province|be|Ісэ (правінцыя)|ckb|پارێزگای ئیسێ|cs|Provincie Ise|de|Provinz Ise|es|Provincia de Ise|eu|Ise probintzia|fa|ولایت ایسه|fi|Isen provinssi|fr|Province d'Ise|gl|Provincia de Ise|hak|Yî-sṳ-koet|id|Provinsi Ise|it|Ise (provincia)|ja|伊勢国|ko|이세국|lt|Isės žemė|nl|Ise (provincie)|pt|Província de Ise|ru|Исэ (провинция)|simple|Ise Province|sk|Ise (provincia)|sr|Провинција Исе|tr|Ise (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Ісе|zh|伊勢國|zh_min_nan|Ise-kok|zh_yue|伊勢國|qid=Q864166}}. <br>
; Yufushu no Mikoto

; Iorihime no Mikoto

=== Sessha ===
The following seven companies that are located in the former {{ill|Yamazaki Village|Q11468104|qid=Q11468104}} village area are considered {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Kyotogaisetsusha}}.
; Mt. Ibe
* Hakusan Hime Shrine - Enshrined on Mt. Inbe, Yamakawa Town, and enshrines {{ill|Izanami|Q682306|qid=Q682306|lt=Isanami no Mikoto}}
* Kunushi Shrine - Enshrined on Mt. Inbe, Yamakawa Town, and enshrines {{ill|Ōkuninushi|Q276944|qid=Q276944|lt=Ōkuninushi no Mikoto}}
; Iwato
* Iwato Shrine - Situated in Iwato, Yamakawa Town, it enshrines {{ill|Ama-no-Iwato-wake no Kami|Q10940542|qid=Q10940542|lt=Amensekimonbetsu no Mikoto}} and Tentatama no Mikoto.
* Takemi Shrine - Enshrined in the same location as Iwato Shrine, Tensoku Tateson and {{ill|Takeminakata|lt=Takeminakata no Kami|UNKNOWN|qid=Q9150391|lt=Takeminakata no Mikoto}} are enshrined here.
* Amamuragumo Shrine - Enshrined in Iwato, Yamakawa Town, it enshrines Amamuragumo no Mikoto and Ijiha Yohime no Mikoto. There is also a theory that it resembles the Shikinai small shrine ``Amamura Kumojin Ijiha Yahime Shrine''.
; eastern foot
* Wakamiya Shrine - Enshrined at the eastern foot of Yamakawa Town, it enshrines {{ill|Omoikane|Q586088|qid=Q586088|lt=Shikaneson}} and Choshiraha no Mikoto.
; Gion
* Odoyama Shrine - Situated in Gion, Yamakawa Town, it enshrines {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|Q272993|qid=Q272993|lt=Hayasu Sanoo no Mikoto}} and {{ill|Kushinadahime|lt=Kushinadahime|Q505469|qid=Q505469|lt=Kushiinada Hime no Mikoto}}.
